presentation.label: LOUDNESS
presentation.summary: A loudness fattener (JClones Fattener) on the DSP: a tuned EQ, a stereo-linked 10:1 compressor with makeup, and a tanh soft clip.
presentation.overview: Fattener makes a track louder and thicker. A highpass clears the subsonics, a peak EQ that COLOR moves from 40 Hz up to 6.7 kHz while raising it to +8 dB tilts what drives the compressor, a stereo-linked 10:1 compressor whose threshold and makeup FAT sets pushes the level up, and a tanh soft clip with a knee COLOR raises from 0.9 to a hard clip at full scale catches the peaks. GAIN drives it all from -24 to +24 dB. It is a buffer-free insert for FX1 or FX2 on any track. This is a source draft: it is not in the catalog or the firmware builder.
highlights: Port of JClones Fattener (MIT), gain-staged for the Octatrack's FX input level: output level within 0.24 dB and distortion within 0.1 dB of the JSFX's
FAT, COLOR and GAIN as in the JSFX, at its defaults
Decays to exact silence: the filters feed their rounding error back, so no whine at full gain
193 cycles/sample, a quarter less than stock SPRING REV per instance; 698 of SPRING REV's 1,063 program words, no buffer
usage: Assign FATTENER in FUNC + FX2 (or FX1) SETUP with LEVEL and YES. It starts at the JSFX defaults: FAT 0, COLOR 0, GAIN 0 dB, which is already a soft compressor.
Turn FAT up for more compression and makeup: louder and denser. Use GAIN to set how hard the track drives it.
Turn COLOR up to move the emphasis from the low end towards the top, and to harden the clip.

controls.name: FAT
controls.doc: Fattness, 0 to 127 = 0 to 100%: compressor threshold -1 to -35 dB and makeup +1 to +40 dB together. 0 is the JSFX default.

controls.name: COLOR
controls.doc: Color, 0 to 127 = 0 to 100%: the EQ from 40 Hz at 0 dB to 6.7 kHz at +8 dB, and the clip knee from 0.9 to a hard clip at 1.0. 0 is the JSFX default.

controls.name: GAIN
controls.doc: Input gain, drawn -64 to +63 for -24 to +23.6 dB in 3/8 dB steps; 0 is 0 dB, the JSFX default.

limitations: Draft only: not in the catalog, configurator or firmware builder until hardware qualification and owner review are complete.
AMP VOL is part of the drive, as the track level into the JSFX would be in a DAW.

For half the DSP time it simplifies the JSFX: one highpass (36.5 Hz) for its 20 + 30 Hz pair, the EQ interpolated between 17 designs (within 0.17 dB), and the compressor's gain computed per 16-sample block and ramped (the envelope still runs every sample).

At FAT and GAIN near maximum the module adds up to 63 dB of gain, so the filters' last bit is amplified too: impulse tails differ from the float model by up to 5e-3 before reaching exact silence within about 0.14 s.
The filter and EQ corners assume 44.1 kHz.
Effect ID 0x0e, priority 20 and layout letter 9 were checked free against the Octamod modules and the TapeHead, IronOxide5 and Inflator drafts only.

The first test image (OCTABAM10) gave CPU overruns on the unit under p-locks and scene moves; this version (OCTABAM11) ran about ten minutes on four tracks under heavy load on the author's MKII without them. Not stress-tested.

storage.label: DSP program
storage.display: 698 words P (473 code, 225 table), 160 words X per instance, no buffer
storage.conditions: Composed build report (both payloads place a 225-word P table and 473 words of code in the 1,063-word donor region). Filter states and errors, the envelope, coefficients, polynomial and tanh tables and staging use $00-$9f of the instance's own r7 block; no allocator buffer, no Y memory. SPRING REV: 1,063 words plus the 16,384-word FX2 instance buffer.

processing.label: DSP estimate
processing.conditions: tools/build/cycle_count.py static count (the frame routine inlined). benchmark.py, executed instructions: one instance 195 per sample (SPRING REV 262); four per core worst 13,536 per 16-sample block (SPRING REV 20,376). With every knob moving every block, 203 instructions per sample in dsp_host. Not a hardware load figure.

impact.conditions: One active instance; every setting costs the same per sample, and COLOR adds about 130 instructions in a block where it changes.

cpu.rationale: No ColdFire code: a DSP insert with a cloned menu descriptor. The ColdFire only forwards three page-1 values.

dsp.rationale: 193 cycles/sample by the static counter, about 6% of the 3,120 cycles/core usable by modules; four per core cost a third less executed instructions than four stock SPRING REVs (benchmark.py). Eight on one core (FX1 and FX2 on four tracks) price at 1,544 of 3,120.

memory.rationale: 698 words of DSP program per payload (code and its table) and 160 words in each instance's existing r7 block. No allocator buffer or Y memory, where SPRING REV takes 1,063 words and a 16,384-word instance buffer.

tests.summary: verify.py renders the assembled module in dsp_host against reference.render_model() (JClones_Fattener.jsfx line for line with the module's three simplifications): peak error 2.1e-3 over ten settings x nine signals at two input levels (within 5 filter LSB times the gain above that), and against the JSFX itself the output level of a sine, a kick and noise within 0.24 dB and its THD at the unit's level within 0.1 dB (gain-staged JSFX(4x)/4). Exact silence (also from a garbage-filled instance block), exact silence again 137 ms after a burst at full gain, stereo link, split calls and cost with every knob moving. The composed test image renders within 6.3e-4 of the model. Benchmarked against stock SPRING REV. Menu, init-register and replace gates pass; MKII emulator LCD captures included. The first build overran on the author's unit under p-locks and scene moves; OCTABAM11 (this source) was played on the author's MKII for about ten minutes on four tracks under heavy load (p-locks and scenes) and reported working great (a listening test, not a stress run).
gates: Worst-case cycles under parameter modulation on hardware
Real hardware stress project: eight audio tracks, at least 60 minutes

access.location: FUNC + FX1 or FUNC + FX2 SETUP on an audio track: the effect chooser (LEVEL selects, YES assigns). The three controls are on the FX main page.
steps: Select an audio track that plays a sample.
Hold FUNC and press FX2 (or FX1) to open its SETUP. Turn LEVEL to FATTENER and press YES to assign it.
Press FX2 (or FX1) to show the main page: FAT, COLOR and GAIN on the top row. The SETUP page has no Fattener controls.
Verified on the MKII panel of the emulator with the hardware test image; not yet on a unit.
